svg.aria-label: Five radar charts, one per upscaler, each with nine spokes; on every spoke the best of the five reaches the outer ring and the others reach in proportion to it, so a larger shape is better and a dent is a weakness. Still picture: accuracy (dB): FSR 4.1.1 44.33 dB, Lossy 44.26 dB, FSR 3.1 39.94 dB, HelixSR 41.99 dB, XeSS 42.14 dB. Moving background: accuracy (dB): FSR 4.1.1 49.27 dB, Lossy 48.98 dB, FSR 3.1 47.95 dB, HelixSR 46.92 dB, XeSS 47.70 dB. Thin railing in motion: accuracy (dB): FSR 4.1.1 41.82 dB, Lossy 41.34 dB, FSR 3.1 38.36 dB, HelixSR 40.12 dB, XeSS 40.86 dB. Areas a moving object has just uncovered: accuracy (dB): FSR 4.1.1 34.48 dB, Lossy 36.45 dB, FSR 3.1 29.22 dB, HelixSR 27.11 dB, XeSS 30.20 dB. Tiny fast sparks: share of their brightness shown (%): FSR 4.1.1 83%, Lossy 74%, FSR 3.1 40%, HelixSR 79%, XeSS 50%. Leaves swaying without motion vectors, mean of three sway speeds: error (of 255): FSR 4.1.1 11.0, Lossy 14.5, FSR 3.1 16.7, HelixSR 14.3, XeSS 14.3. Still picture: change per frame (of 255): FSR 4.1.1 0.037, Lossy 0.024, FSR 3.1 0.014, HelixSR 0.020, XeSS 0.084. Thin wire under a slow pan: change per frame (of 255): FSR 4.1.1 7.2, Lossy 11.0, FSR 3.1 8.2, HelixSR 5.6, XeSS 10.1. Time per upscale call at 3840x2160 (ms): FSR 4.1.1 4.76 ms, Lossy 2.22 ms, FSR 3.1 1.16 ms, HelixSR 1.99 ms, XeSS 4.98 ms.
svg.text: The shape of each upscaler: nine measures
On every spoke the best of the five reaches the outer ring. Bigger is better; a dent is a weakness. Dashed: FSR 4.1.1.
steadiness of a thin wire in a slow pan
A spoke at half length: twice the error (or the change per frame, or the time) of the best of the five; for sparks, half as much shown.
Test rig, 4K output, one card, single runs. This project's exact DLL has FSR 4.1.1's shape with a longer speed spoke (3.17 ms against 4.76).
